newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ABERDEEN APOLOGISE FOR FANS' LACK OF RESPECT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ABERDEEN APOLOGISE FOR FANS' LACK OF RESPECT.

text.p: Aberdeen formally apologised to Scottish premier division rivals Glasgow Rangers on Monday for fans who jeered during a minute's silence for former Rangers' and Scotland captain George Young.

Aberdeen chairman Ian Donald urged his club's fans to report anyone who they knew to be responsible for the jeering, which occurred before Rangers' 4-0 win at Ibrox on Sunday. About 1,000 Aberdeen supporters were at the match.
Young, capped 53 times for Scotland, died on Friday aged 74.
Rangers' manager Walter Smith said: "I thought it was terrible. It is the worst thing I have heard in football in Scotland for a long time."

The atmosphere at Rangers-Aberdeen clashes has deteriorated markedly in recent seasons. Last month a missile was thrown at the Rangers' team coach outside Aberdeen's Pittodrie ground after Smith's side won 3-0.
Two years ago Rangers' striker Mark Hateley was attacked outside Pittodrie while team mate Ally McCoist once had a golf-ball thrown at him during a match between the two clubs.
